app.title: EEG Quality Inspector
app.summary: A person loads a multichannel recording, either a synthetic demo with known artifacts or an uploaded EDF or CSV file. For a CSV they must state the sampling rate and units. They look over the stacked per-channel waveforms, choosing which channels to show and narrowing to a time window. They then read a per-channel table of quality indicators: missing samples, flat windows, amplitude exceedances and possible clipping. The table puts flagged channels first and recomputes whenever they change a threshold in the sidebar. They check each channel's power spectrum, with an optional 50 or 60 Hz line-noise ratio, and finish by downloading a self-contained HTML report and a CSV of the metrics.

task.text: Find which channels of a multichannel recording have recording problems, using explainable indicators with adjustable thresholds, and export a report of what was found.

data.text: A multichannel signal recording sampled uniformly over time and converted to one voltage unit, with a per-channel table of computed quality indicators and power spectra.
data.item: one channel of a multichannel recording

stage.text: screening raw EEG recordings for recording problems after acquisition, before analysis

mechanism.text: Sidebar controls load the recording and set the thresholds. Four tabs then show the same recording as stacked per-channel waveforms with a channel picker and time-window slider, as an indicator table that recomputes when a threshold changes, as overlaid power spectra with a line-noise check, and as an export page with downloads.

field.text: signal quality checks on EEG recordings in electrophysiology

workflow.name: screen a multichannel recording for quality problems and export a report

steps.here: Load the seeded synthetic demo, or upload an EDF file (units come from its header) or a CSV (the sampling rate and units must be stated). Size, rate and duration limits are checked before loading.

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: Stacked per-channel traces on a shared time axis. A channel multiselect and a time-window slider narrow what is drawn.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: For each channel, compute missing samples, the flat-window fraction, amplitude exceedances and possible-clipping runs over 1-second windows. The table sorts flagged channels to the top.
Sidebar inputs set the flat peak-to-peak limit, the amplitude threshold and the minimum clipping run. The indicators recompute at once without reloading the data.
Welch power spectra for all channels are overlaid on a log axis. An optional 50 or 60 Hz selector shows each channel's line-noise ratio against neighbouring bands.
Download a self-contained HTML report (plots, thresholds, units, missing-data accounting) and a CSV of the per-channel metrics.

distinctive: Analysis runs in nonoverlapping 1-second windows. Windows containing missing samples are excluded and counted, never interpolated, and a channel with no usable window is marked unavailable.
Waveforms are thinned for display by binning that keeps each bin's extremes, the reduction is shown on screen, and the analysis still uses every sample.
Units are never guessed. A CSV needs the units stated, an EDF's units are read from its header, and channels that are not voltage are excluded with a notice.
The indicators are descriptive flags with visible thresholds and no good/bad verdict. The line-noise check is offered only when its frequency bands fit below Nyquist.
A seeded synthetic demo with a known artifact on each channel lets a person try every check without a file.
